Update: A day later, GPT-6 Astra is gradually rolling out to Business and Pro customers on subscription plans of US$100 and US$200 per month respectively. This is the release arrangement for other new models before Plus customers gain access on their US$20 monthly plan.

It has been just over a year since OpenAI first launched the GPT-5 model for ChatGPT. Now it's GPT-6 Astra's turn to enhance ChatGPT and Codex capabilities. Details below.

GPT-6 Astra Details

OpenAI officially introduces its new model, GPT-6 Astra, calling it "the world's smartest and most coherent model."

OpenAI further elaborates on how GPT-6 improves computer operation capabilities, allowing ChatGPT to control your Mac or other desktop computers, including running in the background while you work:

In addition, OpenAI states that GPT-6 Astra is "the best software engineering model to date."

For Codex, here are GPT-6's new features:

OpenAI calls GPT-6 Astra "a significant leap in cybersecurity capabilities," noting it has "reached a critical threshold for cybersecurity under the Preparedness Framework."

For this reason, the model will be rolled out to users gradually.

OpenAI says: "Starting today, GPT-6 Astra will be available first to select organizations, and will roll out to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users over the coming days. It is also available via the OpenAI API and AWS."

"Astra usage is included in existing subscription tiers, and users and enterprises can purchase additional usage credits. Pro, Business, and Enterprise plan users will have access to GPT-6 Astra Pro. Enterprise admins can enable Astra for their workspaces; it will be off by default at launch."

The Journey Toward GPT-6 Astra

GPT-5 launched on August 7, 2025, replacing GPT-4o and several reasoning models to become the default model in ChatGPT. Its biggest feature is automatic routing: ChatGPT can answer instantly or activate deeper reasoning as needed. OpenAI also claims it produces fewer factual errors than GPT-4o.

Apple adopted the model in iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS Tahoe 26. ChatGPT requests handled through Apple Intelligence, including Siri handoffs, Writing Tools, and Visual Intelligence features, switched from GPT-4o to GPT-5.

GPT-5.1 in November promised warmer, more natural responses. GPT-5.2, launched in December under a "red alert" triggered by Gemini competition, accelerated professional work efficiency. GPT-5.3 Instant addressed ChatGPT's "awkward and stilted" tone, and two days later GPT-5.4 Thinking debuted with a million-token context window and built-in computer operation capabilities.

OpenAI subsequently added GPT-5.4 mini and nano, the restricted GPT-5.4-Cyber, GPT-5.5 for higher-autonomy work, GPT-5.5 Instant, and the GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna models launched in July.

From the Codex Mac App to the All-New ChatGPT

The software around these models has also undergone innovation. OpenAI launched a dedicated Codex Mac app in February, serving as a central platform for running multiple coding agents, reviewing changes, and scheduling work.

In July, Codex essentially replaced the original ChatGPT desktop app, integrating chat, work, and Codex into one, while the previous native client was renamed ChatGPT Classic.

For me, Codex has completely transformed how I use ChatGPT. I can delegate more work that doesn't require critical thinking, and even build tools on my Mac that I previously couldn't.

GPT-6 Availability

OpenAI says the new GPT-6 model will initially only be available to members of its cybersecurity-focused Daybreak program. This is similar to the previous release cadence for GPT-5.6.
